sub_indicators.label: Access to information law
sub_indicators.subject: gov.legislate
sub_indicators.text: Access to information legislation: access to information law
sub_indicators.norm_short: The African Commission's 2019 Declaration of Principles sets out a right of access to information, a duty to publish and an independent oversight body set up by law. Its 2013 Model Law on Access to Information is the template.
criteria: A source from the past three years says the country has no access to information law and no draft of one. A right of access written in the constitution alone is not a law.

A bill or draft exists: published, validated, out for consultation, before cabinet or parliament, or passed and not yet promulgated. A law that is only announced, planned or called for does not count.
An access to information law is in force, however old: an act, ordinance or decree with the force of law that gives a right to ask public bodies for information.
The law has been put to work: a decree, regulation or order made under it, or its information commission or commissioner set up, or an existing body it names taking up the oversight.

The law has been applied in the past three years: a decision, order or penalty by the oversight body or a court, published figures of requests or complaints, or a rule made under the law. Training, an awareness campaign or an oversight body merely existing does not reach this stage.

aspects.name: Law put to work and applied
